Appearance:
 Shri Sudhanshu Vyas - Advocate for the petitioner.
Shri Amit Rawal appearing on behalf of Advocate Gene  ORDER Heard.

02. This petition has been preferred by the petitioner being aggrieved by the order dated 11.02.2025 (Annexure P/3) passed by respondent No.2, the Deputy Director and Authorized Officer, Food Safety and Standards Act, whereby his license for running a meat shop has been cancelled.

03. Learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted that the aforesaid order has been passed by respondent No.2 without issuance of any show cause notice to the petitioner, without affording him any opportunity of hearing and in violation of the principles of natural justice.
Even as per Rules, an opportunity of hearing ought to have been given to the petitioner.

Since the same has not been done,
the impugned order deserves to be set aside.

04. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondents/State has submitted NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:7146 2 WP-8251-2025 that under the Rules, the respondents have the right to cancel license as has been done in the present case without issuance of any show cause notice.
It is further submitted that against the impugned order, the petitioner has the remedy of preferring an appeal under the rules itself.
The petition hence deserved to be dismissed.

sentences.text: I have considered the submissions of learned counsel for the parties and have perused the record.
06. Admittedly, prior to passing of the impugned order, no notice was issued to the petitioner to show cause against the action proposed to be taken against him.
By the impugned order, license of the petitioner has been straightaway cancelled.

As per Rule 2.1.8(4) of Khadya Suraksha aur Manak (Khadya Karobar ka Anugyapan aur Registrikaran) Viniyam, 2011, a license can be cancelled with immediate effect if the same is necessary for public health.

entities.text: Khadya Suraksha aur Manak (Khadya Karobar ka Anugyapan aur Registrikaran) Viniyam, 2011
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, in the present matter, license of the petitioner has been cancelled on the ground that by running of his meat shop, there is discontent in the villagers and there is possibility of arising of law and order situation.
The same cannot by any stretch of imagination be said to be a matter concerning public health.
The said clause is hence wholly inapplicable to the facts of the present case.
07. As per Clause 2.1.8(1)(3) of the aforesaid Rules itself, prior to suspension of the license and prior to cancellation of the same, a notice is mandatorily required to be issued to the licensee.
The case of the petitioner is governed by these provisions.
Notice was hence mandatorily required to be issued to him prior to suspension of his license and cancellation of the same.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:7146 3 WP-8251-2025
However, no show cause notice has been issued to the petitioner.
In fact his license has not even been suspended and thereafter cancelled but has been cancelled straightaway.
The same is in gross violation of the principles of natural justice and the specific rules having been framed in this regard.

In such circumstances, the ground of availability of alternate remedy to the petitioner to challenge the impugned order by preferring an appeal is not liable to be entertained and is accordingly rejected.
08.

As a result, the impugned order dated 11.02.2025 (Annexure P/3) is hereby quashed with a further direction to the respondents to pass a fresh order after giving due opportunity of hearing to the petitioner and issuing proper show cause notice to him.
With the aforesaid direction, the petition stands allowed and disposed off.
